analytic.title: Towards a Minimum Initial Marking Estimation Procedure for P-Time Labelled Petri net Systems

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: This work develops a technique for estimating the minimum initial marking (an initial marking with the minimum total token number) of a real-time system modelled by a P-Time labelled Petri net system under partial observation. Indeed, the set of events is partitioned into a set of observable events, which can be detected by an external agent and a set of unobservable ones. Furthermore, some observable events can be associated to the same observation, i.e., they produce the same output signal and are called undistinguishable. In addition, the obtained marking must be consistent with a given label occurrence vector (LOV). The proposed method is based on an iterative procedure combined with a schedulability analysis technique for particular behaviors of the studied system.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Petri nets (PN on short) [1] are a graphical and mathematical modeling tool applicable to a large variety of systems. They have proven to be effective to model, analyze, and control real time and automated manufacturing systems that are characterized as being concurrent, asynchronous, distributed, parallel, nondeterministic, and/or stochastic.

Tokens are used in these nets to simulate the dynamic and concurrent activities of systems. As a mathematical tool, it is possible to derive state and algebraic equations, and other mathematical models governing the behavior of the considered systems.

As the size and complexity of real man-made systems increase, significant attention is devoted to problems of state estimation in PN models. Indeed, it is practically impossible to associate a dedicated sensor to each variable of interest of the modelled plant.

In this paper we discuss the problem of estimating the minimum initial marking (MIM in short) of a real-time system modelled by a P-Time labelled Petri net system based on event observation. Furthermore, this MIM has to be consistent with a given label occurrence vector (LOV). Indeed, this LOV can be seen as a firing count vector associated with the labels (sensor output signals) of the system. For example, in part production settings, minimum resource allocation involves the determination of the smallest number of resources required to complete a given event sequence of machine operations.

In this context, the authors of [2], [3] present an algorithm for obtaining a marking estimate for a given PN based on complete knowledge of the observed firing sequence but without knowledge of the initial state.

In [4] the authors consider the marking estimation problem based on the observation of a sequence of transition labels in a given labelled PN with known initial marking. They show that, under some conditions on the structure of the PN, the set of markings consistent with the observed label sequence can be captured by a linear system whose size does not depend on the length of the observed label sequence. Li et al., [5] study the least-cost planning sequences estimation problem. Their algorithm captures the evolution of possible marking(s) through the observation of labels sequence. Indeed, the marking evolution is guided with low cost transition firing sequence(s) consistent with a given sequence of labels. The authors in [6] deal with the MIM problem in labelled PN, the main idea of their algorithm is to gather markings which can be associated with similar firing count vector and to keep the MIM in this set, at every observation of a new event. They proposed a recursive algorithm of polynomial complexity in the length of the observed label sequence. Basile et al., [7] develop an algorithm to estimate the marking of a time PN with unobservable transitions. Thanks to the introduction of a so-called modified state class graph the main information on the possible behaviors of the considered system is obtained. Ye et al., [8] propose a polynomial algorithm to solve the initial tokens allocation problem in the context of structurally live Petri nets with inhibitor arcs. An heuristic algorithm is developed in [9] to solve the minimum initial marking problem in the context of untimed Petri nets. Furthermore, the obtained solution is associated with a given firing count vector.

The problem studied in this paper is the following: given a set of events which can be converted into a set of labels sequence that needs to be accomplished, find the minimum initial marking (i.e., the minimum initial number of resources needed) that allows the completion of these events while adhering to the time constraints imposed by the associated P-time labelled PN.

In this work we assume that the P-time labelled PN structure is known while the initial marking is not. Moreover, the set of transitions (i.e. events) is partitioned into a set of observable and unobservable ones. Furthermore, some observable events can be associated to the same label, then, they are called undistinguishable.

The complexity of the proposed method is generally exponential in the size of the given set of event. Indeed, we have a finite number of sequences of event and each one has a finite number of transition firing sequences (that correspond to a given sequence of labels ).

The paper is organized as follows: a brief reminder of the basics of untimed Petri nets followed by a formal definition of P-Time Petri nets (P-TPN) and labelled P-Time PN (P-TLPN) is realized in the next section. Section three covers the procedure of schedulability analysis of particular behaviors. The problem statement and the proposed algorithm for the determination of the minimum initial marking is tackled in section four. An illustrative example is proposed in the fifth one. Finally, in the last section some conclusions and future work are presented.

div.head: A. Untimed Petri Nets
div.p: It is assumed that the reader is familiar with Petri nets, in the following only the basic notions are recalled. If it is not the case, please refer to [1].

A Place/Transition net (P/T net) is a structure N = (P, T, P re, P ost), where P is a set of m places; T is a set of n transitions. P re : P × T → N and P ost : P × T → N are the pre and post incidence functions that specify the arcs; C = P ost -P re is the incidence matrix. The preset and postset of a node X ∈ P ∪ T are denoted • X and X • . A marking is a vector M : P → N that assigns to each place of a P/T net a non-negative integer number of tokens, represented by black dots. M (p) is the marking of place p.

A net system N ; M 0 is a net N with an initial marking M 0 . A transition t is marking enabled at M if M ≥ P re(•, t). A transition t enabled at M may fire, yielding the marking M = M + C(•, t). A marking M is reachable in N ; M 0 iff there exists a firing sequence σ such that M 0 [σ > M . The set of all sequences that are enabled at the initial marking
div.formula: M 0 is denoted L(N, M 0 ) i.e., L(N, M 0 ) = {σ ∈ T |M 0 [σ >}.
div.p: The set of all markings reachable from M 0 defines the reachability set of N ; M 0 and is denoted R(N, M 0 ).

div.p: In a P-TPN, a transition sequence σ = t 1 t 2 . . . t s is said to be schedulable if all transitions in σ are schedulable in the given order. So, it exists a set of markings M 1 , M 2 , . . . , M s such that (M 0 t 1 M 1 t 2 . . . t s M s ) is a feasible sequence in the underlying net and t i , i ∈ {1, . . . , s} is schedulable under M i-1 . If at least one transition in σ is non schedulable then σ is non schedulable. In a P-TPN, the schedulability of a transitions sequence is verified with regard to the timing constraints associated with the model places. In the underlying PN of a P-TPN, denoted UPN, a marking is said to be reachable if there exists a firing sequence (M 0 t 1 M 1 t 2 . . . t s M s ), or simply an occurrence sequence δ = (t 1 t 2 . . . t s ) which leads to marking M s starting from the initial marking M 0 . If a transition sequence is not an occurrence sequence in the UPN, it can't be schedulable in its associated P-TPN. Nevertheless, an occurrence sequence in the UPN is not necessarily schedulable in the associated P-TPN because of the timing constraints.

In a P-TPN, the sojourn time (i.e., the amount of time that a token has been waiting in a place) is counted up as soon as the token has been dropped in the place as seen previously. div.p: The developed technique is based on an iterative procedure. Indeed, it will process iteratively the components of V l ( ): if the first processed symbol is b then V Sol (O bs ) will become [101] and the MIM allowing to produce observation O bs = b on P-TLPN N P will be searched for (in the sequel, the notation V Sol (O bs ) -b will be adopted). At the end of the procedure the firing sequence(s) (schedulable on P-TLPN N P ) consistent with the observation associated with the original given LOV will be computed along with the minimum initial marking producing this observation.

At Step 5, being given an observation O bs ∈ Ω the set SEQ(O bs ) will be defined as follows:
div.formula: SEQ(O bs ) = {σ ∈ T |P o (σ) = O bs }.
div.p: Indeed, the set of firing sequences consistent with the current studied observation is computed.

At step 6, the minimum initial marking for each the previously computed firing sequences is evaluated. This evaluation is realized thanks to a recursive technique presented in [2], [3] and further exploited in [6]. It is based on an initial marking update procedure computed for a given firing sequence σ by providing the smallest number of tokens allowing to enable each transition. Indeed, the initial marking is updated each time a transition of σ fires by adding to its input places the necessary token(s). It represents the starting point for the minimum marking computation (initialization phase).

At step 9, the boolean variable IMPROVEMEN T initialized at TRUE (at step 2) will be set to FALSE (at step 17) when no improvement will be further possible (over the set of considered firing sequences). Thus, an improvement is realized (for a firing sequence) when the current solution (in terms of marking) is better than the previous one -i.e., a new marking M new is obtained at the current step (say, j + 1) with M new < M old and M old obtained at the previous step (say, j).

At step 10, each considered firing sequence will go through a mutation operation for any undistinguishable transition that it contains. For instance, let consider an alphabet Ω = {a, b} with T = {t 1 , t 2 , t 3 } and LM(t 1 ) = LM(t 2 ) = a, LM(t 3 ) = b (t 1 and t 2 are undistinguishable). If the current observation is O bs = ab and initially, SEQ(O bs ) = {t 1 t 3 }. The mutation operation will lead to the MIM computation for sequence t 2 t 3 which will be compared for the one obtained for t 1 t 3 .

div.head: VI. CONCLUSIONS AND FUTURE WORK
div.p: In this paper, an estimation method for the MIM of real-time systems modeled by P-time labelled Petri nets is presented. In particular, the model considered is made of both observable and unobservable transitions which can share the same label (i.e., they are undistinguishable), adding a non-determinism source to the studied problem. The proposed method is based on an iterative procedure coupled with a schedulability technique. It allows to evaluate, each time a label is observed, the feasible candidate firing sequences that have the initial marking estimate with the smallest total number of tokens. Indeed, thanks to the proposed algorithm the experimental results show that a reasonable approximation of MIMs with faster running time than the method proposed in [6] can be obtained.

Unfortunately, the proposed procedure faces the combinatorial state space explosion problem because of its exponential complexity. Consequently, several directions to improve the applicability and reduce the complexity of the developed procedure are left for future investigations.
